AlphaGrep Securities Private Limited is a quant trading firm with a focus on algorithmic
trading across global asset classes. With offices in Mumbai, Bangalore, Gurgaon,
Singapore, and London, we are among the largest firms by trading volume on Indian
exchanges and hold significant market share on several major global exchanges. Our
approach is rooted in a disciplined and systematic quantitative methodology aimed at
identifying factors that consistently generate alpha. These factors are integrated with
our proprietary ultra-low latency trading systems and robust risk management
practices to formulate trading strategies spanning equities, commodities, currencies,
and fixed income, actively traded on global exchanges.

Engineering group. This team designs in-house trading applications that are robust and
extremely fast.
Responsibilities
●
Design, develop, and test proprietary software, including:
Trading strategy simulation software optimized for distributed computation
Large-scale data acquisition, storage, accessibility, and visualization
Real-time trade management and risk analysis.

Identify innovative solutions to complex problems and advocate for their
implementation by clearly and concisely communicating your ideas to the team.

Collaborate with other software developers, quantitative traders, and
researchers in cross-functional team environments.

mathematics, and related fields to apply. Additional requirements include:

Excellent Software Development knowledge, demonstrated through

entries.jobDescription:
Domestic (bangalore/hyderabad), 10 weeks summer internship,
Our quantitative & technical engineers are at the cutting edge of our business, solving
real-world problems through a variety of analytical methods. Working in close
collaboration with bankers, traders and portfolio managers across the firm, their
invaluable quantitative perspectives on complex financial and technical challenges
power our business decisions. As a member of our team, you will use your advanced
training in mathematics, programming and logical thinking to construct quantitative
models that drive our success in global financial markets. Your talents for research,
analysis and aptitude for innovation will define your contributions and enable you to
find solutions to a broad range of problems, in a dynamic, fast-paced environment.
Whatever your background, you will bring a fresh perspective and unique skill set to
our business. In return, you will be trained by our experts across the firm to navigate
the complexities of the financial markets and state-of-the-art methods in quantitative
finance. An ordinary day is anything but. You may work on alpha-generating strategies;
discuss portfolio allocation problems; and build models for prediction, pricing, trading

automation, data analysis, and more. Whichever your area of contribution, your ideas
will have a measurable effect on our business and on our clients. Candidates would be
required to work on a wide range of problems, including the following: Developing and
validating quantitative models used:
1) to calculate the fair value of financial contracts (securities and derivatives)
2) to measure, analyze and manage the risks in our businesses (market, counterparty
credit, operational, funding, and liquidity risks as well as legal, regulatory, and
reputational risks)
3) to execute trades and make markets electronically in equity and fixed income
products and
4) to create trading strategies, portfolio analytics, and risk management tools for the
firm’s mutual funds, hedge funds, and private wealth clients.
Designing and developing sophisticated software and systems using proprietary as
well as modern web, mobile, and, desktop technologies:
1) To manage, visualize, and analyze massive sets of the market and operational data
used in our trading, risk management, and control functions.
2) To correctly and efficiently route orders for billions of dollars of securities every day
3) To allow the ability to represent, transact in, and risk management all of the firm’s
OTC derivative positions
4) To distribute computations across tens of thousands of computers.
5) To make use of functional programming paradigm and big data solutions to develop
firm’s next generation modeling, pricing, and risk management platform
6) To contribute to key open source initiatives– e.g. GSCollections, Project Panama
7) To build the firm's strategic mobile platform.
entries.testAndInterview:
The test had some math problems, basic probability problems and three coding
questions interlinked with each other. 1st round:
●
Started off with "tell me about yourself".Then 2 probability problems for the rest
of the interview.
●
First question was based on Russian roulette (standard question).
●
Second question was based on expected /average value (similar to a brainstellar
problem) but had 2 dice instead of 3. Tip: build up your approach step by step
(i.e., first solve for one, two then 3 dice)
●
 er was interested in the student approach to solve the question, even
if they didn't arrive at the actual answer.
2nd round:
●
The second round was conducted by a senior member of the company and
started with HR-style questions, such as "Why finance?" and "What have you
done related to finance?" Extensive finance knowledge was not required, and
the questions were based on the candidate's responses.
●
 er was interested in the quant finance IDDD offered by IIT Madras
(Student had taken that)
●
After the HR-style questions, the interviewer presented a puzzle involving a dog
and five doors.( Each night, the dog moves from one door to an adjacent door,
and we do not know the dog's initial starting point. The challenge was to devise
a strategy to find the dog, similar to problems found on Brainstellar.)The
 er was open to providing assistance if needed.
●
The interviewer ended the interview open to questions.

entries.testAndInterview:
Coding test on data structures and algorithms Round 1:
●
Starts off with questions on various topics to gauge your experience with these.
Sample questions are:
○
When would you use a binary search tree instead of an array/linked list?
○
Difference between threads/processes
○
Difference between hashing/encryption
○
What is DNS
○
Difference between index/primary key

●
This is followed by DSA questions. Explanation of the algorithms followed by a
Python implementation is expected.
Round 2:
●
Questions on courses that you are doing currently and your interest towards
these courses are asked.
●
System design questions are asked, to mainly check communication and
reasoning skills rather than proficiency and knowledge.
●
Some DSA questions may be asked, such as: You are given a non-directed
acyclic graph. You play as red, your opponent is blue. All nodes in this graph are
initially unpainted. At the beginning, you pick a node and paint it red. Then, your
opponent picks a node and paints it blue. Now, the game proceeds as follows:
○
Every turn, you pick an unpainted node adjacent to a red node, and paint
it red.
○
Your opponent picks an unpainted node adjacent to a blue node, and
paints it blue.
○
This happens until neither of you can make a move.
○
The winner is whoever has more nodes painted in their colour.
How do you play optimally? Write an algorithm to find the correct starting node.
(Do it in O(n)).

weeks immersed in the fast-paced, dynamic world of market making. As Optiver's
Software Engineer Summer Intern, you'll fully own projects that directly impact
Optiver's world-class trading systems. Experience the thrill of tight feedback loops and
shipping your code to production. Receive feedback from our senior Traders, and
receive mentorship from the industry’s best and brightest technologists. This is your
chance to make a direct impact on a leading trading firm, while launching your career in
engineering. If you’re looking to work in a challenging international environment and
have a passion for solving complex problems, apply today to kick-start your future.
What you’ll do As a Software Engineer intern, you'll work side-by-side with your

mentor to build latency-critical applications that directly improve the market. From day
one you’ll tackle real issues that need to be solved through projects that further
develop and optimize our systems. Each day will bring new challenges requiring your
fresh perspective. You'll own end-to-end projects, from developing to testing to
shipping your code to production. It's an unrivaled opportunity to accelerate your
knowledge and make your mark on Optiver's core business. You will also have the
chance to join industry lectures to learn about trading and our other departments to
gain a complete understanding of Optiver and our business. Don't worry, you won't be
expected to have previous knowledge of the financial industry! You'll be educated and
upskilled by our world-class trainers in order to hit the ground running.

The performance of our systems – profiling and optimizing our software and
hardware

Developing tools in close collaboration with our traders to improve our trading
strategies

Building a powerful tool to find errors in our systems by turning huge amounts
of data into useful information In all cases you can expect that all projects will
be a valuable contribution to our business, focusing on actual issues that we
face and like to see solved. The internship will jump start your career! Who you
are

You are a penultimate year student with ability to work full-time upon
graduation in 2025

You have a desire to step outside your comfort zone and face fresh challenges
every day
●
You have a passion for technology and an interest in the financial industry

You enjoy solving complex problems and can clearly articulate solutions both
verbally and written

You are proficient in either C++ or Python
What you can expect from us is an energetic and collaborative work culture with
ambitious, down-to-earth colleagues. We constantly ask ourselves how to do better,
which creates a stimulating and fun environment. To be concrete:

An 8-week internship taking place in May 13, 2024 – July 5, 2024

Mentoring and feedback from senior engineers on how to write clean, lean and
pragmatic code, and solve complex problems with simple solutions

Competitive salary: €40,000EUR total compensation over the 8 week period
(~₹35,90,320.00 INR)

(Paid) furnished housing arrangement provided by Optiver in the city center of
Amsterdam

Awesome social events and outings (boat tours through the canals of

Most importantly, the possibility to receive a full-time offer upon completion of

s:

The business case study is slightly different. A situation is given and there are several

entries.about:
Jane Street
 the Position:
As a Quantitative Trading intern, you’ll be part of an immersive experience, paired with
experienced Traders who will teach you how we identify market signals, analyze and execute
trading strategies, construct quantitative models, conduct statistical analysis, and build trading
intuition.
During the program you’ll work on projects that expose you to the wide variety of problems,
we solve every day. Interns have the chance to be mentored sequentially by full-time
employees working in two different areas of trading.
Quantitative Trading interns work on a diverse range of projects with their mentors, conducting
studies on new or existing datasets, building quantitative models, writing new tools, or even
considering big-picture questions that were still trying to figure out. Project work is
complemented by classes on the broader fundamentals of markets and trading, lunch
seminars, and dozens of simulated interactive trading sessions.
A profitable trading strategy is only as strong as the technology it runs on, and we consider
ourselves as much a technology company as a trading firm. While exposure to a particular
programming language is not required, general programming experience is a plus.

If you’d like to learn more, you can read about our interview process and meet some of our
newest hires.
https://www.janestreet.com/join-jane-street/interviewing/
https://www.janestreet.com/join-jane-street/get-to-know-us/
 You:
We don’t expect you to have a background in finance or any other specific field—we’re looking
for smart people who enjoy solving interesting problems. We’re actually more interested in
how you think and learn than what you currently know. You should be:
- A strong quantitative thinker who enjoys working collaboratively on a team
- Eager to ask questions, admit mistakes, and learn new things
- Fluent in English

As our Quantitative Trading Intern, you’ll spend your summer tackling complex, 
quantitative problems at one of the world’s leading tech-driven trading firms. 
Under the guidance and mentorship of industry experts, you’ll apply your strong 
reasoning skills to design, develop and enhance our innovative trading strategies, 
fully immersing in the world of market making. 
From derivative theory training to hands-on trading experience, you’ll have 
deepened your understanding of the quantitative trading industry by the end of the 

7 
8-week internship. Plus, if you’ve excelled during the program, you’ll receive an 
offer to return as a Graduate Quantitative Trader. 
Note: The Mumbai internship program will take place in our Sydney office. Travel and 
accommodation expenses will be covered by Optiver. 
What you’ll do 
Requiring a pragmatic mindset, logical problem-solving skills and mathematical 
precision, our internship is as close as you can get to a real trading experience. Led 
by our dedicated in-house education team that consists of ex-traders and 
engineers, our Quantitative Trading Internship offers you the opportunity to: 
· Complete our curated series of lectures and coursework on trading 
fundamentals, covering topics such as options pricing, financial markets, 
trading strategies and cutting-edge technology. 
· Apply your recently acquired knowledge in a simulated trading 
environment, trading options using live market data for a realistic hands-on 
experience. · Analyse real historical data to develop your own algorithmic 
trading strategy and backtest to see how it performed. 
· Learn directly from our team of full-time educators and current traders, 
gaining exposure to our various trading desks and experience the financial 
markets first-hand. 
· Test your potential and accelerate your growth in a fascinating and 
high-performing environment.

As a Software Engineering Intern at Optiver, you’ll work alongside experienced 
engineers to develop innovative solutions that enable us to respond to the financial 
markets at lightning-fast speeds. In just a few weeks, you could develop 
latency-critical applications that contribute towards our trading success. 
By the end of the 8-week internship, you’ll have deepened your understanding of 
how technology is used in the quantitative trading industry. Plus, if you’ve excelled 

11 
during the program, you’ll receive an offer to return as a Graduate Software 
Engineer. 
Note: The Mumbai internship program will take place in our Sydney office. Travel and 
accommodation expenses will be covered by Optiver. 
What you’ll do 
Led by our in-house education team that consists of ex-traders and engineers, 
you’ll delve into advanced engineering concepts and lead innovative projects, 
during our world-class training program. Whether it's developing ultra-low latency 
exchange protocol encoders and decoders, or fine-tuning our automated trading 
strategies and pricing models, you’ll work closely with traders and other engineers 
to build simple, well-architected solutions that meet the needs of our business. 
You’ll experience the excitement of a fast-paced development cycle – owning a 
tight feedback loop, testing and shipping your code to production. You could be 
working on a change to a trading system in the morning and see it run live by the 
afternoon. No two days are the same, and it’s up to you and your team to drive our 
success in the ever-evolving capital markets. 
Aside from technical skills, our dedicated education team will also work with you 
on your development, including: 
●
Workshops on a variety of tech-based topics, along with soft skills to 
support your holistic growth as an engineer. 
●
A dedicated mentor who will guide you through our development 
process and how our trading systems work. 
●
Trader training to get you up to speed on our business. This helps you 
understand the fundamentals of trading, enabling you to make an impact 
from the early stages of your Optiver career.

entries.testAndInterview:
and Interview: 
The scholarship test was relatively tough and consisted of two sections, each of 
one-hour duration. The first section was based on mathematics, quantitative aptitude, 
and logical reasoning, while the second section covered coding, OOPs, operating 
systems, and computer networks. The top 20 candidates were shortlisted for s and awarded the scholarship.
 
 Two interview rounds were conducted, both online via Google Meet, each with a 
single panelist. The first interview, for the quant profile, focused on quantitative 
concepts, including questions from mathematics and statistics, along with a 
challenging quant problem. The candidate approached one problem using a 
brute-force method (substituting values from 1 to n) due to difficulty in identifying the 
underlying logic. Additionally, a question on multithreading and race conditions was 
asked.
 
 The second interview was primarily a sanity check, where three questions similar to 
those in the scholarship test were asked. A DSA question was also included, where the 
 er expected both brute-force and optimal approaches at a conceptual level, 
without requiring actual code. Although some questions were more aligned with SDE 
roles, they were included as part of the evaluation. The interview concluded with a 
discussion on five key qualities expected of a quant researcher at the candidate’s stage.

was followed. Additionally, 50 Challenging Problems in Probability by Frederick

entries.jobDescription:
Software Development Engineer -Internship 
At Amazon, we hire the best minds in technology to innovate and build on behalf of 
our customers. The intense focus we have on our customers is why we are one of the 
world’s most beloved brands – customer obsession is part of our company DNA. Our 
interns write real software and collaborate with a select group of experienced 
software development engineers (SDEs) who guide interns on projects that matter to 
our customers. 
As an intern, you will be matched to a manager and a mentor. You will have the 
opportunity to influence the evolution of Amazon technology and lead mission critical 
projects early in your career. Your design, code, and raw smarts will contribute to 
solving some of the most complex technical challenges in the areas of distributed 
systems, data mining, automation, optimization, scalability, and security – just to name 
a few. 
In addition to working on an impactful project, you will have the opportunity to engage 
with Amazonians for both personal and professional development, expand your 
network, and participate in activities with other interns throughout your internship. No 
matter the location of your internship, we give you the tools to own your project and 
learn in a real-world setting. Many of our technologies overlap, and you would be hard 
pressed to find a team that is not using Amazon Web Services (AWS), touching the 
catalogue, or iterating services to better personalize for customers. 
If this opportunity interests you, apply and come chart your own path at Amazon. 
By applying to this position your application will be considered for all locations we 
hire for in India. This includes but is not limited to Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, 

66 
Delhi and Pune. Amazon internships are full-time (40 hours/week) for six months 
with start dates between January and February 2026 (as per university academic 
framework). 
 
Key job responsibilities 
• Collaborate with experienced cross-disciplinary Amazonians to conceive, design, 
and bring innovative products and services to market. 
• Design and build innovative technologies in a large distributed computing 
environment, and help lead fundamental changes in the industry. 
• Create solutions to run predictions on distributed systems with exposure to 
innovative technologies at incredible scale and speed. 
• Build distributed storage, index, and query systems that are scalable, 
fault-tolerant, low cost, and easy to manage/use. 
• Ability to design and code the right solutions starting with broadly defined 
problems. 
• Work in an agile environment to deliver high-quality software. 
Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. For an update on your status, or to 
confirm your application was submitted successfully, please login to your candidate 
portal. 
NOTE: Amazon works with a high volume of applicants so we appreciate your patience 
as we review applications. 
Basic qualifications 
• Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree in Computer Science, 
Computer Engineering, or related field at time of application 
• Familiarity with the syntax of languages such as Java, C/C++ or Python. 
• Knowledge of Computer Science fundamentals such as object-oriented design, 
algorithm design, data structures, problem solving, and complexity analysis. 
Preferred qualifications 
• Previous technical internship(s). 
• Experience with distributed, multi-tiered systems, algorithms, and relational 
databases. 
• Experience in optimization mathematics such as linear programming and nonlinear 
optimization. 
• Effectively articulate technical challenges and solutions. 
• Adept at handling ambiguous or undefined problems as well as ability to think 
abstractly.

technology. Founded in 2015 and 
headquartered in Gurugram, we operate across diverse asset classes—including

The process typically consisted of 3–4 interview rounds with 1–2 panelists per round, 
conducted either online or offline.

JEE-level Mathematics.

Tries, LCA, Number Theory, Binary Lifting, and basic OOPs.

concepts, while SWE roles focused more on DSA, live coding, OOPs, and Computer 
Architecture. s were often easier than the tests and largely revolved around 
problem-solving, coding, projects, and resume discussions. 
Live coding and pseudocode-based problem solving were common; interviewers often 
evaluated approach, communication, and code quality rather than just the final 
answer. Be prepared to discuss your projects in depth, including implementation 
details, technical decisions, and underlying concepts.

entries.preparationMaterials:
● DSA: Striver DSA Sheet, Ultimate DSA Sheet, 450 DSA Cracker, LeetCode, 
GeeksforGeeks, Codeforces, and CSES (especially DP, Graphs, Trees, 
Searching & Sorting). 
● Competitive Programming: Regular CP practice was widely recommended 
for both tests and interviews. 
● Probability: 50 Challenging Problems in Probability, Heard on the Street, 
Brainstellar, Dice Problems, and the Green Book.

senior guidance.

entries.suggestions:
● Start preparation early (ideally 2–3 months before the internship season) and 
focus on building strong fundamentals. 
● Practice coding and problem-solving consistently; DSA mastery comes from 
solving a large number of problems and learning from mistakes. 
● Maintain a record of problems you could not solve initially and revisit them 
later to reinforce patterns and concepts. 
● Pay close attention to corner cases, debugging, and understanding why 
solutions fail. For quant-oriented roles, prepare Probability, basic ML concepts, 
and introductory Finance topics such as bonds, Sharpe ratio, and stock prices. 
● Build a strong resume and be thoroughly familiar with everything 
written on it. During interviews, stay confident, communicate your 
thoughts clearly, and demonstrate your problem-solving process. 
● The process can sometimes feel unpredictable; focus on preparation 
rather than shortlists or outcomes, and maintain good mental resilience. 
● Explore both off-campus and on-campus opportunities instead of relying on 
a single route. 
● Put in consistent effort, trust the preparation process, and keep a positive 

92 
mindset throughout.

entries.testAndInterview:
and Interview: 
The interview process consisted of three rounds, with a strong emphasis on 
quantitative reasoning, probability, mathematics, and analytical thinking. The first 
round focused heavily on probability concepts and challenging puzzle-based questions 
that tested logical reasoning and problem-solving skills. The second round further 
explored probability and calculus-based concepts while also assessing understanding 
of Deep Machine Learning topics and their practical applications. The final round was 
comparatively more conversational and centered around behavioral assessment, 
strategy modelling, and statistical concepts. The overall process evaluated both 
technical depth and the ability to reason through complex problems. Interviewers were 
particularly interested in understanding the logic behind candidates’ approaches rather 
than simply arriving at the correct answer. Candidates who could clearly explain their 
reasoning, assumptions, and decision-making process performed well throughout the s.
entries.preparationMaterials:

Statistics, and Machine Learning was crucial for preparation. Resources such as 
NeetCode were useful for strengthening DSA problem-solving skills, while academic 
coursework such as MA2040 provided a solid foundation in probability theory. Regular 
practice of probability-based questions, puzzles, and quantitative reasoning problems 
proved especially beneficial for handling interview-style questions. In addition, prior 
experience through internships, projects, startups, or work with established 
organizations helped candidates discuss real-world applications of analytical and 
modelling concepts more effectively during interviews. 

148
entries.suggestions:

formulas or solutions. Interviewers often probe the reasoning behind answers, making 
conceptual clarity significantly more important than rote learning. Ensure that every 
project, internship, or experience listed on the resume can be explained confidently and 
in detail. For aspiring candidates targeting quantitative or analytical roles, prioritize 
DSA, Probability, Mathematics, and problem-solving skills, as these form the core of 
most assessments. Practice a variety of probability and puzzle-based questions, 
strengthen statistical intuition, and cultivate the habit of explaining your thought 
process logically. A clear understanding of concepts combined with strong analytical 
reasoning can significantly improve performance throughout the selection process.

entries.preparationMaterials:

entries.suggestions:
1. In DSA, people concentrate more on learning the language and Data Structures, 
but my opinion is that Algorithms are the most important part of it. So preparing 
this is most important, and Data Structures can be learnt alongside this.
2. Vibe coding while practicing is not helpful. Though some people use it for only 

206 
the "programming" part of their work and give the logic themselves, this would 
negatively impact them in the test and interview processes where they have to 
code without any external help.
3. Logic is the most important part of an Algorithm. Don't just learn how to 
implement an algorithm, it's important to learn how it WORKS. Almost never would 
they ask to blindly implement an algorithm, it would be an extension of it, to do this 
you need to know how an algorithm actually works.
4. People pay too much attention to Codeforces Rating, number of problems solved 
on Leetcode and such, but in my experience none of this matters at all. Some 
companies do ask this, but it will only be used in some edge case scenarios only. 
What matters mainly is your performance in the OAs and the Interview, so knowing 
the theory, intuition and practice of programming is enough, not a 1900 rating on 
Codeforces.
5. When you see a new problem/algorithm in an OA, prepare it so that if at all it 
repeats in the next OA, you will be able to do it. The number of repeated questions 
in the OAs are surprisingly high, so more often than not, the prep of unknown 
problems in OAs will be more useful than plain preparation.
6. Read the blog that I will write soon that is more personalised towards prep/ info 
regarding Atlassian.
7. Try to read the interview experience from platforms like medium, gfg as much as 
possible and prepare accordingly.

entries.testAndInterview:
● The online test is strictly based on Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA). 
● There are no aptitude, logical reasoning, or core computer science subject questions. 
● It typically consists of 2 to 3 coding questions. ● Total Rounds: Up to 3 rounds (2 Technical, 1 HR) for candidates who make it to the 
end. The interview lengths can be extensive, with total time across all rounds 
reaching up to 4 hours. 
● Round 1 (Technical): Deep focus on basic to medium DSA. Usually involves 1 or 2 
questions (LeetCode Easy to Medium/Hard). Heavy emphasis on Trees and Graphs 
(e.g., colored binary tree variants, finding the minimum path between two nodes in a 
tree). Each round takes roughly an hour. 
● Round 2 (Technical): A continuation of technical problem-solving, testing topics like 
Backtracking and Dynamic Programming (DP). Also takes about an hour. 
● Round 3 (HR): Standard HR questions, only for those who clear the first two 
technical rounds.
entries.suggestions:
● Soft Skills: High-level soft skills aren't strictly evaluated; simply practicing problem 
discussions with friends is enough to communicate effectively with the interviewer. 
● Tech Focus: Don't stress too much about hardcore Competitive Programming (CP) 
concepts during the interview; strong, foundational DSA is usually sufficient. 
Preparation Material: 
● Standard Sheets: The Striver A-Z DSA Sheet (or Ultimate DSA Sheet) is the most 
highly recommended resource. 
● Platforms: LeetCode and NeetCode for practicing standard DSA problems. 
 
 

 
 
● Advanced Practice: For an extra edge (and to help with resume shortlisting), solving 
Codeforces problems (specifically in the 1400-1600 rating range) is recommended. 
● Key Topics to Master: Trees, Graphs, Dynamic Programming (DP), and Backtracking.

entries.testAndInterview:
● The initial round was a 24-hour Kaggle challenge where candidates were required 
to train an ML model and submit their predictive CSV file 
● Note: Because the total number of applied candidates was low, the company 
relaxed the filtering and directly shortlisted everyone for the interview round 
anyway, though the submission was a formal part of the track ● Consisted of 1 single, extensive Technical interview round that lasted over 1 hour 
and 10 minutes 
● The interview content was highly dependent on the interviewer's background and 
the candidate's resume: 
1. For this candidate: The focus was on Classical Machine Learning (explaining 
Bagging vs. Boosting, Dimensionality Reduction concepts, and why they are 
necessary). 
2. Resume Deep-Dive: The candidate had a Driver Drowsiness Detection System on 
their resume. The interviewer asked deep operational questions about frame 
extraction logic and how the system dynamically observes physical behavioral 
changes from frame to frame. 
3. Additional Core Topics: Included basic Python syntax questions (specifically 
dictionary-based manipulations) and fundamental DBMS/SQL questions. 
4. What other candidates faced: Depending on the specific panel, other applicants 
were heavily questioned on Deep Learning fundamentals (Transformers, LSTMs) as 
well as Generative AI trends like Agentic AI and RAG (Retrieval-Augmented 
Generation). 
● Difficulty Level: Rated around 3.5 to 4 out of 5 (Significantly thorough, but 
manageable if fundamentals are clear).
entries.suggestions:
● Do Not Bluff on Your Resume: Never include extra tools, skills, or advanced projects 
with the mindset of "learning them on the way." Interviewers can pick absolutely 
any word from your resume and drill deeply into it. It is perfectly fine to have a 
shorter resume as long as you have complete mastery over everything written on it. 
● Be Ready to Pivot: If an interviewer is inclined toward a technology they personally 
work on but you haven't mastered, clearly communicate what you have worked on 
so they can redirect their questions to your area of strength. 
● Stay Updated with Modern AI Tech: For Data Science and AI roles, alongside 
standard Machine Learning and Deep Learning, focus heavily on current industry 
concepts like Agentic AI and RAG, as a vast majority of newer roles are looking for 
these skills. 
● Embrace Interview Rejections as Practice: Don't be disheartened by early failures. 
Treating real interview rejections as iterative practice is one of the most organic 
ways to build robust soft skills and refine your delivery. 
● Start as Early as Possible: Do not wait for an ideal timeline. Keep practicing standard 
DSA consistently, and polish your core domain-specific tech stack well in advance.

entries.about:
the Firm: Guna Solar is a premier solar EPC firm specializing in high-performance 
rooftop and ground-mounted energy engineering arrays for commercial and industrial (C&I) 
clients, balancing data-driven physical design and financial tracking models. 
● Project Framework: C&I corporate consumers showcase wildly divergent power load 
curves. This project aims to design and build an advanced computational 
decision-support tool that executes the following blocks: 
1. Simulates solar PV generation vectors mapped against Battery Energy Storage 
System (BESS) reactions across real-world consumption load libraries. 
2. Optimizes physical battery capacity configurations, charge/discharge cycle 
depths, and real-time power dispatch rules. 
3. Formulates technical behavior to structural financial parameters: computing 
exact Internal Rate of Return (IRR), ROI profiles, asset payback timelines, and 
battery degradation curves. 
4. Automates individualized sizing blueprints dynamically linked to localized 
customer utility grid tariffs and historical load steps. 
Key Responsibilities & Deliverables 
● Create a Load Curve Library of 8–10 industry-specific energy profile tracks. 
● Simulate underlying system layouts using Python, MATLAB, or multi-variable Excel 
modeling architectures. 
● Model battery cycle efficiencies, environmental degradation variables, and expected 
asset lifespans. 
● Track utility cost savings stemming from automated load shifting, peak grid demand 
charge reduction, and immediate solar self-consumption optimization. 
● Expected Deliverables: Code validation for 5 separate industrial load configurations; 
a working prototype software engine generating sizing options with precise cash flow 
projections; tool regression tests verified against historical case metrics. 
Selection Process & Compliance Mandates 
● Selection Process: Interview-only; no online tests or coding challenges. 
● Group Discussion: Not applicable.

Exhaustive Interview Round Log 
● Round 1 & Round 2 (ML Knowledge & Resume Grinding): Highly intensive technical 
rounds focused on portfolio validation and project code architecture. The interviewers 
explicitly adjust questioning to match the candidate's declared background. If a 
candidate has limited theoretical knowledge, they grill the basic fundamentals and

scenario-driven rather than simple definitions (e.g., “What happens if we make this 
specific structural change in your pipeline?”, “Does the model performance get better, 
or does it degrade under this constraint?”), looking closely for logical analytical 
reasoning. Both rounds heavily place a premium on clear, structural, and articulate 
explanations.

Lead. This final round shifts entirely away from AI/ML engineering domains or 
technical metrics. Instead, it features highly abstract puzzle-type questions designed 
to evaluate raw mental flexibility, open-ended problem-solving intuition, and 
adaptive thinking under pressure. 
● Strategic Prep Advice: Formally enrolling in or reviewing rigorous institutional AI/ML 
courses provides an immense backdrop advantage. Building unique, customized 
projects addressing actual deep learning or NLP challenges provides a definitive edge 
over generic, template-based resumes. Comprehensive expertise across all subfields 
is not mandatory if your structural fundamentals are rock solid. Never drop into a rigid 
argument or combative debate against your interviewer. Focus on cleanly 
understanding their optimization hints, explicitly state your design hypotheses, and 
always treat the session as a co-collaborative technical discussion.

● Core Technical Rounds: The 3 to 4 live video evaluation sessions do not dwell

into probability logic, statistical theory, combinatorics, and general mathematical 
problem-solving. The panel thoroughly evaluates your first-principles calculation 
accuracy and mental scaling flexibility under live pressure. 
● HR Fitment Round: A brief, conversational final validation checkpoint evaluating 
corporate cultural alignment, long-term career aspirations, and team collaboration 
frameworks. 
● Strategic Prep Advice: Since the interview track is heavily driven by probability and 
math in general, brushing up on high-level distribution frameworks, expected values, 
linear algebra matrices, and permutation/combination patterns is absolutely vital to 
clear this review pipeline. Extensively practice abstract logic puzzles and mental 
probability constraints using curated quantitative interview guides (such as Heard on 
the Street or The Green Book). Ensure you can effortlessly discuss and dry-run your 
backend programming logic in Python or C++, highlighting how you manage or clean 
large, complex historical datasets.
